controls.label: Initial amount N0
controls.help: Sets the initial amount N0 that multiplies the remaining fraction f, scaling the remaining amount N(t) while leaving the exponent lambda*t, the fraction and the half-life unchanged.

controls.label: Decay constant lambda
controls.help: Sets lambda; a larger lambda raises the exponent lambda*t, lowers the remaining fraction f and the remaining amount N(t), and lowers the half-life ln 2 / lambda.

controls.label: Elapsed time t
controls.help: Sets the elapsed time t; a larger t raises the exponent lambda*t, lowers the remaining fraction f and the remaining amount N(t), and leaves the half-life unchanged.

explorations.title: Doubling the decay constant
explorations.instruction: Predict: if lambda doubles while N0 and t stay fixed, what happens to the remaining fraction, the remaining amount and the half-life? Then apply the preset, which sets lambda to 0.1 1/y.
explorations.observe: The exponent readout rises from 1 to 2, the remaining fraction falls from 0.3679 to 0.1353, the remaining amount falls from 3.679 mol to 1.353 mol, and the half-life falls from 13.86 y to 6.931 y.
explorations.why: Doubling lambda doubles the exponent lambda*t at the same t, so the exponential exp(-lambda*t) is squared and the fraction drops from 0.3679 to its square 0.1353; the amount inherits the same factor, and the half-life ln 2 / lambda is halved because it carries lambda in its denominator.

explorations.title: Slow versus fast decay at the same time
explorations.instruction: Predict: at fixed N0 = 10 mol and t = 20 y, how do a slow decay constant and the default decay constant differ in remaining fraction, remaining amount and half-life? Then apply the preset, which sets lambda to 0.01 1/y.
explorations.observe: The exponent readout falls from 1 to 0.2, the remaining fraction rises from 0.3679 to 0.8187, the remaining amount rises from 3.679 mol to 8.187 mol, and the half-life rises from 13.86 y to 69.31 y.
explorations.why: A smaller lambda multiplies the same elapsed time into a smaller exponent lambda*t, so exp(-lambda*t) stays closer to 1 and much more of the sample remains; the longer half-life ln 2 / lambda shows that the same curve is stretched over a much longer time.

invariants.name: fraction stays within zero and one
amount stays nonnegative and no larger than the largest allowed N0
exponent stays between zero and lambda max times t max
half-life stays between ln 2 over the largest and smallest allowed lambda
